evals.prompt: I just finished a round of changes in both repos/ai-stock-analysis and repos/portfolio-website, and the personal-os main repo hasn't been bumped yet. Please run an integration preflight and list a safe order for wrapping this up. Read-only checks only — do not commit, push, reset, or discard any dirty changes.
evals.expected_output: A read-only multi-repository preflight report that distinguishes parent gitlinks from actual child HEADs and dirty files, identifies the validation order, and gives safe next actions without mutating Git state.
expectations: The response checks root status and submodule status separately.
The response distinguishes a recorded parent pointer from the child repository's actual HEAD and worktree state.
The response explicitly preserves dirty or untracked child changes and does not recommend reset, checkout, clean, or stash as an automatic repair.
The response proposes an ordered validation and pointer-update sequence.
The response follows the project's Status vocabulary and gives a structured integration report.

evals.prompt: This change touches scripts/lib/wealth, web/lib/report.ts, and config/wealth_rules.yaml, and also updates ai-stock-analysis. Help me judge whether it can be merged into the main repo, and list the contracts, tests, and public/private boundaries that must be checked. Do not commit on my behalf.
evals.expected_output: A contract-aware integration review covering Python ownership of valuation, the Python/TypeScript report contract, config freshness, submodule readiness, public/private separation, and focused verification gates.
expectations: The response identifies Python as the owner of wealth valuation/report mathematics and TypeScript as a consumer.
The response calls for a Python-to-TypeScript report contract or fixture check.
The response checks config/wealth_rules freshness and source metadata rather than treating the YAML as unquestioned truth.
The response checks that private holdings and profile data do not cross into public market or public submodule paths.
The response lists focused tests and explicitly says no commit is performed.

evals.prompt: I only changed .agents/skills/wealth-manager and docs/plan-wealth-dashboard.md, and now I want to commit. First do a repo preflight for me, and tell me when it should be handed off to git-commit and when it shouldn't be.
evals.expected_output: A focused single-root preflight that checks skill/doc references and trigger ownership, detects whether submodule or contract checks are unnecessary, and clearly hands off only after the user has explicitly requested a commit.
expectations: The response scopes the change to skills and documentation instead of inventing unrelated submodule work.
The response checks skill frontmatter, referenced paths, privacy placeholders, and stale terminology or plan status.
The response distinguishes a preflight from the git-commit skill's staging and commit responsibilities.
The response does not stage or commit files during the preflight.
